beaker.definition: A flatbottomed jar made of glass or plastic.

flask.definition: The quantity a flask will hold.

test-tube.definition: A slender glass or plastic container holds, combines, or warms small liquid samples in laboratory experiments.

pipette.definition: Measuring instrument consisting of a graduated glass tube used to measure or transfer precise volumes of a liquid by drawing the liquid up into the tube.
pipette.exampleUsage: The pipette was used during the activity.

graduated-cylinder.definition: A narrow glass or plastic container has numbered marks for measuring liquid volume with reasonable accuracy.

petri-dish.definition: A petri dish is a laboratory instrument used to grow microorganisms in a controlled environment.
petri-dish.exampleUsage: The petri dish was used during the activity.

funnel.definition: A conically shaped utensil having a narrow tube at the small end.

burette.definition: Measuring instrument consisting of a graduated glass tube with a tap at the bottom.
burette.exampleUsage: The burette was used during the activity.

erlenmeyer-flask.definition: An Erlenmeyer flask is a laboratory instrument used to measure and control the temperature of solutions.
erlenmeyer-flask.exampleUsage: The erlenmeyer flask was used during the activity.

volumetric-flask.definition: A volumetric flask is a laboratory instrument used to measure and control the volume of solutions.
volumetric-flask.exampleUsage: The volumetric flask was used during the activity.

watch-glass.definition: Used in laboratories, a watch glass is a shallow dish for evaporating liquids or covering a beaker.

dropper.definition: Pipet consisting of a small tube with a vacuum bulb at one end for drawing liquid in and releasing it a drop at a time.

microscope.definition: Magnifier of the image of small objects.

bunsen-burner.definition: A Bunsen burner is a laboratory instrument used to heat and vaporize substances.
bunsen-burner.exampleUsage: The bunsen burner was used during the activity.

centrifuge.definition: An apparatus that uses centrifugal force to separate particles from a suspension.

hot-plate.definition: A portable electric appliance provides a hot surface for heating, cooking, or keeping food warm.

scale.definition: A device that measures how heavy a person or object is.
scale.exampleUsage: The scale was used during the activity.

thermometer.exampleUsage: The thermometer was used during the activity.

ph-meter.definition: An electronic device measures a solution’s acidity or alkalinity by sensing hydrogen-ion activity and reports the result on the pH scale, typically from zero to fourteen.
ph-meter.exampleUsage: The ph meter was used during the activity.

spectrometer.definition: Spectroscope for obtaining a mass spectrum by deflecting ions into a thin slit and measuring the ion current with an electrometer.

incubator.definition: Apparatus consisting of a box designed to maintain a constant temperature by the use of a thermostat.

fume-hood.definition: A fume hood is a laboratory instrument used to protect workers from harmful fumes and vapors.
fume-hood.exampleUsage: The fume hood was used during the activity.

lab-coat.definition: Protective outerwear worn over ordinary clothes in a laboratory helps shield the wearer from spills and contaminating substances.

safety-goggles.definition: Protective glasses worn to guard the eyes.

latex-gloves.definition: Latex gloves are a type of protective gear used in laboratory settings to protect hands from chemicals and oils.

face-shield.definition: A clear protective covering worn over the face to help keep droplets or splashes away from the eyes, nose, and mouth in schools, laboratories, and healthcare settings.

fire-extinguisher.definition: A portable or fixed device that releases a suitable substance to put out or contain a small fire.
fire-extinguisher.exampleUsage: The fire extinguisher was used during the activity.

eyewash-station.definition: An eyewash station is a laboratory instrument used to remove or neutralize bodily fluids.
eyewash-station.exampleUsage: The eyewash station was used during the activity.

chemical-shower.definition: An emergency safety shower used to rinse hazardous chemicals from a person's body or clothing.
chemical-shower.exampleUsage: The laboratory safety tour pointed out the chemical shower.

first-aid-kit.definition: A portable set of medical supplies and equipment provides immediate help for minor injuries or sudden illness while professional care is unavailable.

hazard-sign.definition: A sign that warns people about a possible danger or unsafe condition.
hazard-sign.exampleUsage: The hazard sign identified a corrosive-material area.

clamp.definition: To fasten or fix with a clamp.

ring-stand.definition: A heavy laboratory stand with a vertical metal rod used to support clamps, rings, and equipment.
ring-stand.exampleUsage: The clamp was attached securely to the ring stand.

stirring-rod.definition: A thin rod, usually made of glass, used to stir liquids in laboratory containers.
stirring-rod.exampleUsage: The student used a clean stirring rod to mix the solution.

mortar-and-pestle.definition: A bowl and club-shaped tool used together to crush or grind solid materials.
mortar-and-pestle.exampleUsage: The sample was ground gently with a mortar and pestle.

scalpel.definition: A thin straight surgical knife used in dissection and surgery.
scalpel.exampleUsage: The glossary uses the term "Scalpel" in an educational description.

forceps.definition: An extractor consisting of a pair of pincers used in medical treatment (especially for the delivery of babies).

syringe.definition: To spray or irrigate (a body part) with a syringe.

magnifying-glass.definition: A handheld tool uses a curved lens to make nearby details appear larger for close viewing or reading.
magnifying-glass.exampleUsage: The magnifying glass was used during the activity.

acid.definition: Any of various water-soluble compounds having a sour taste and capable of turning litmus red and reacting with a base to form a salt.

solution.definition: A homogeneous mixture of two or more substances.

indicator.definition: (chemistry) a substance that changes color to indicate the presence of some ion or substance.

reagent.definition: A chemical agent for use in chemical reactions.

sample.definition: Items selected at random from a population and used to test hypotheses about the population.

specimen.definition: A bit of tissue or blood or urine that is taken for diagnostic purposes.

slide.definition: A smooth surface children slide down for fun.

stain.definition: To color with a liquid dye or tint.

crystal.definition: A protective cover that protects the face of a watch.

lab-notebook.definition: A ready-made notebook layout for recording an experiment, with sections for its purpose, materials, method, results, and conclusion.

graph-paper.definition: Paper printed with a regular grid helps you plot data and draw graphs.

calculator.definition: A device used for doing mathematical calculations.
calculator.exampleUsage: The calculator was used during the activity.

computer.definition: A machine for performing calculations automatically.
computer.exampleUsage: The computer was used during the activity.

data-chart.definition: A visual display uses bars, lines, or pie sections to present numbers and other information, making patterns easier to interpret and analyze.

timer.definition: A device that measures or signals the end of baking time.
timer.exampleUsage: The timer was used during the activity.

label.definition: A radioactive isotope that is used in a compound in order to trace the mechanism of a chemical reaction.

barcode.definition: A set of contrasting lines and spaces allows a scanner to identify a product and access its information.

log-sheet.definition: A form or page used to record events, measurements, checks, or activities in order.
log-sheet.exampleUsage: The technician entered the temperature on the log sheet.

report.definition: A written document describing the findings of some individual or group.

autoclave.definition: A device for heating substances above their boiling point.
autoclave.exampleUsage: The autoclave was used during the activity.

compound.definition: Composed of more than one part.

catalyst.definition: (chemistry) a substance that initiates or accelerates a chemical reaction without itself being affected.

solvent.definition: A liquid substance capable of dissolving other substances.

enzyme.definition: Any of several complex proteins that are produced by cells and act as catalysts in specific biochemical reactions.

analyze.definition: To make a mathematical, chemical, or grammatical analysis of.

synthesize.definition: To combine so as to form a more complex, product.

calibrate.definition: To make fine adjustments or divide into marked intervals for optimal measuring.

filter.definition: To remove by passing through a filter.

extract.definition: To extract by the process of distillation.

sterilize.definition: To remove or kill microorganisms on an object or surface.

document.definition: A digital file containing written or visual information.

peer-review.definition: A structured classroom exercise brings students together to read one another’s drafts and offer constructive feedback that improves the writing.
